title: aura kingdom
text: I have to say first off that my opinion may be considered biased as this was the first mmo rpg that I  truly loved. I had played WoW previously and couldn't stick with it, so when I saw this game I was less than optimistic, however I am jubilant to inform you that this game captured both my attention as well as my imagination. Part of this is the art style, I am a huge fan of anime in general and this games aethestic was the whole reason I started my adventure as an envoy of Gaia. But my love for anime wasn't the only artistic point within this game, the enemies that you encounter are well designed and truly fun to throw down with, not only that but the areas and dungeons in this game are so beautiful and imaginative that it's hard not to just stare around at random pretty scenes going "oooh" and "ahhh". Another strong point in this game are the eidolons that follow you about, helping you beat the local wildlife into lumps of exp. The eidolons are a core focus of the game, you start the game with one of four, I always choose Merilee the cheery silph, others include a dragon, a floating boy, and a unicorn straight out of my little pony. The eidolons are upgradable too, so they progress with you, and can be passed around between your charecters at will, as long as they're not assigned to a charecter already. The final good point I'm going to make, I had a few more but I'm getting lazy, is the games intricate story, now on the outside this game looks cutezie and nice, but read some diologue and you quickly realize this game is about as serious as knee surgery. Espionage, robberery, demons, a scandolouse love story in the second area, and the tragic tale of a theif, whom I will not name. It's a real shame that most people skip the diologue, it's rich and interesting and makes the game much better than withought it, ie nothing would make any sense. Now for the bad news, if you want endgame, too bad. Of course  there's the sky tower a raid right in the main hub of the game, and with the most recent update came the sky realms, of which I know nothing about because my internet recently gave out. I love this game but the severe lack of endgame content needs to be fixed. Another negative is the gut renching grind your looking at if you want eidolons that you can't get through the story. Basically you need key fragments, 8 of them if my memory serves, now that doesn't sound bad until you realize that to get the key fragments you have to defeat that eidolon in boss form only to realize that the drop rate for the fragments are ridiculously miniscule. In short only go for eidolons you really want. Or just pay for the keys in the game store with real money.... My final point of negativity is the charecter levels 60-62. If your a veteran you know what I mean, dear lord it takes so much to get to lv 62, you have to do both areas unlocked at these levels twice to three times through to gain the necessary exp. It takes way too long to go up those two levels. Well I hope you find this review helpful, please give this game a chance, it's great and it needs more love from Western players. Thanks for reading.

title: aura kingdom
text: Aura Kingdom is one of those games that is kinda boring when you first start playing, but once you sit and play it more and more, it can start being more and more fun as you get into it, and discover the game more. At the very beginning of the game, you are introduced to the very core of the game, quests and combat, but as you progress you are able to do more, like fishing, archeology, cooking, card dueling, and many more. You are able to discover more about your eidolon where each eidolon has their own personality. On top of that there are a decent range of classes to play as, ranging from magic, to assasins to a really strong knight. This game has a class for everyone, and you can create 3 different characters when you first open up the game. This game has a lot of effort put into it, and so there is so much personality in it. This is a game where it doesn't matter if you want to play with a group or go solo, you can do either. If you want to be in a group go out there and find a guild, meet some people, if you want to play solo, you can make it so you don't see anyone else but you. This game has a lot to offer and so much to explore, it is one of the best mmorpg games i have ever played. It's a kind of game where you can do almost anything. Its not long before you can fly around, and that makes it easier to explore. The quests make you travel every map so your not missing out on anything. One thing about it though is that if you think the game is getting annoying because why would you need to do something, its most likely the fact that you are able to skip the text and plot. Meaning if you care little about plot, there's that for you, or you can read what every character says, and learn the value of these characters you meet, and understand why you need to do things that you wouldn't think you needed otherwise. I love this game and if you don't thats fine but the least i ask is to try it because its free, and why not, cause when i first saw this, i didn't think i'd like it, a month later i got it, and now about 4 months later, i love it having so many hours on it, and still loving every part of it. And I hope that you will to.

title: banished
text: Rain on your window Tea on your desk Perfect conditions for some Banished! From my personal gaming experiences, this game mostly relates to The Settlers. You build a village while managing resources and population. The major difference being that Banished does not contain any warmaking and it is in fact faster-paced. And as you probably already noticed from other people's reviews, the game is quite a challenge at first. The learning curve is steep. Really steep. The tutorials don't really teach you how to play the game, but merely how to use the UI. You learn the game mechanics through playing the game... and failing at it. My first clear learning moment was when my 20-something population village suddenly started to die off due to old age. I quickly learnt the importance of houses, which you need to build to control population growth. Too many houses can cause your village to grow too fast and lead to severe famine due to too little workers and too many children. With too few houses on the other hand, the aging of population may catch up. The second learning moment was when I struggled with food production. My food reserves started dropping and nothing managed to get it up again. I was even having 18 workers gathering food out of a total population of just above 20. This taught me a lesson on building locations. Food gatherers need old trees to gather food, and multiple hunting locations is important as well. After your first couple of village failures, you get the hang of it. Your villages become more successful and robust against anything the game can throw at you. If your village is finally self-sustainable, there is really nothing more to it than to expand. Increase population, expand food production, repeat. Although the learning curve is steep, it is really not that high. There are only a limited number of buildings. And it gets a bit dull over time. When you need to expand food production, you can decide to build another hunter... or farmer... or a fisherman perhaps? The choices really are limited. Yes, there are a dozin different types of fruit and vegetables you can farm, but why do these even make a difference? The crop fields or orchards basically all look the same. I am missing more and diverse buildings. Eventually the game misses a purpose. When your village is striving, nothing really gives you any goals to expand it even further. There are some achievements to be earned, but that may never be a substitute for a lack of gameplay. Unfortunately this is a disease of modern-day games, achievements do not equal gameplay! It is really amazing that his game was created by a single developer. The game concept is great and it is executed well. The game in its current state is fun and enjoyable, but I still see a lot of room for expansion and improvement. Long term game objectives, buildings and features can still be added and I would strongly recommend the developer to do so. This game will keep me busy for many more rainy weekend hours to come!

title: bastion
text: For some reason, it took me 3 separate attempts over a few years to actually sit down and play this game all the way through. After finally finishing the game, I have to admit I'm not quite sure what held me back on my first 2 attempts because Bastion is a truly great game. It succeeds in nearly every way. Probably the most noteworthy and distinct aspects are its narration and visuals, both of which players will notice almost immediately. The narration guides along not only the story, but the gameplay as well, which - when coupled with the source of the narration - provides a more intimate and closely-felt experience. Much of the game's worldbuilding and lore is also developed through the narrator, with his very human, down-to-earth, and often heartfelt voice acting. Characters and their backstories are also developed in this way, and the story being progressed in this manner turns out to be more intricate and poignant than it would seem at first. Worldbuilding also takes place quite literally as the world is built before your eyes as you move along an area. This decision to have the setting come to life as you go does wonders for the feel of the game; it's a design choice (and in a way, a mechanic) that is entirely unique and refreshing and elevates the aesthetics of the game to another level. Also worth mentioning is Bastion's incredible soundtrack. Its varying tracks fit the moods of different moments and locations exceptionally well. The music of Bastion is instrumental ( ) in creating the right atmosphere as it complements the narration and aesthetics to make a truly powerful experience. One track in particular caught my attention the instant the female vocals rang out, and I almost stopped playing just to appreciate the chillingly beautiful song. The actual gameplay of Bastion is probably its weakest point, and that's only because the rest of the game is on another level. The gameplay is actually quite good, with satisfying combat that holds more depth than it would initially seem. It's not as amazing as Bastion's other aspects, and it doesn't really do anything new, but it works just fine for the game and still provides for a fun experience. There is also a fair amount of replayability, which is always a plus in my book. With a gorgeous soundtrack and aesthetics, solid gameplay, and top-notch narration, Bastion easily deserves its spot in the hall of fame for indie games. 8.5/10

title: batman™: arkham knight
text: So while this game has had a hard first few months, it finally got its patch. With this new patch, preformance was increased, the 30 fps cap is now an optional setting in graphics tab, and stuttering is minimum if you set settings to ones that match your PC build (but still consistant). Now to the breakdown. +The characters, enemies and allies, are very well designed and voiced +This Batman game adds many new mechanics listed below +Batmobile/vehicle's make for awesome gameplay +New enemies, from Medics that revive enemies to brutes weilding Miniguns +New abilites, such as the Fear Takedown and Counter-throw +Have a helper during combat, for new items/abilities and duel takedowns +The map is large, filled with enemies and interesting side-quest +The AI is more adaptive with the Militia, such as radio checkins, seeing into and grenading vents, and drones +Selecting side-quest is a breeze with the new mission select wheel +The game is just amazingly beutiful -The game seems to lag more during batmobile chases, prefer to roam by glide to reduce lag -The game still lags a lot, and stuttering still occures -As far as I've seen so far, you cannot switch characters (i.e. Robin, Nightwing) outside of their missions, making them one-time characters, making their unique weapon-loadout pointless -PC controls are terrible, either adapt or use a consol controller PC adapter like I use -Some side-quest are very short, and makes me wishing they would make them longer +The story was decently long, and interesting +Scarecrow and the Arkham Knight made great main-enemies +The Arkham Knight is a well-design character, personality and preformance wise +Has a good few twist in the story -One detective-mode crimescene in the entire main story, and a few mini-detective-mode crimescene's in sidequest. Wtf WB Games? They were one of the funnest parts!!! The game was very enjoyable to play overall. However, one feature that I really enjoyed from previous Arkham games, the Detective Crime scanes were lacking, very disappointed by this. The Batmobile made a heavy impact on the game, in both quest and campaign, making up for lack of detective work. This is, what I believe, to be a great ending to the Batman: Arkham series, however with WB games taking its sweet time releasing the patch, I feel like the PC version is dead and unrevivable. EDIT: With the refund option now avalible for everyone, no matter the hours played, I would recommend to refund the game for PC. While I do not recommend the game for PC, I do recommend the game for console if avalible.
